reviews.comment: Dr. Kaya was a good professor and explained materials very clearly. I found 207 to be easier to manage due to his style and lectures. I would recommend this professor. Just be ready to work on homework, as the exams are manageable if you follow up with homework.

Genuinely one of the best professors I've ever had. I've heard horror stories about PHYS207, but Dr. Kaya turned it into my favorite class ever. He's very eager to answer any questions and ensure that topics are well understood, and his lectures are incredible, makes you understand things on a deeper level. His tests are super reasonable too.

Your professor in 206 only really matters for lecture quality, and in that regard Dr. Kaya is great. He encourages questions and dedicates each lecture before an exam to review. Don't let it take away from the fact that the exams still require intense work outside of class to do well.

He's ok, I get why some people like his way of teaching, but I honestly found it boring, the first weeks were fine but then it became more boring and boring, I didn't see the passion for him to teach this class.

Fantastic guy! Not an exciting lecturer. I would take him to avoid a bad prof. He does iClickers pretty rarely. He works problems out in class so come if you need reinforcement for the homework. The exams are devastating but not his fault since they're common. He does genuinely care, but the content is just difficult. You either get it or you don't

Your professor in University Physics only matters for lecture quality, and all assignments and exams are common. In that regard, Dr. Kaya did a fine job. He was receptive to questions and dedicated each lecture before an exam to review and working through practice problems.

He is a very caring and approachable professor who is easy to talk to during office hours. However, be prepared for a disconnect between lectures and exams. He spends a lot of class time on long conceptual derivations, which didn't leave enough time to cover the specific material needed for the departmental common exams.

Kaya is an incredible teacher. Though I got a B, it's definitely not because of him. Exams are ridiculously hard, and the classwide averages for the final three exams were all failing. There's lots of homework and extra stuff to boost grades, so use those. He does reviews before each exam, and encourages questions no matter how silly they sound.

University PHYS 206 is a HARD course, but Kaya is a great teacher if you pay attention. Though I got a B, it's not Kaya's fault. Put in some serious effort and an A is attainable. He does reviews before each exam.

Clear and concise lectures, very example-heavy, so you have many opportunities to apply theorems in practice. He prepares us very well to take the 4 exams we have throughout the semester, but the studying responsibility will still 100% fall on you, so don't slack off. Homework is long and challenging, so don't put it off until the last minute.
reviews.ratingTags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: This is a very difficult class no matter who you have. Dr Kaya is nice but doesn't do much since there are two course leaders. Lectures are very theoretical and I would be lying if I said I learned very much from them. Sweet guy who is always looking for questions to answer. Go to his OH though he is very helpful 1 on 1.

Ali Kaya is an ok lecturer; he explains the topics of the course decently. The problem is that he does not prepare you for the common exams, often opting to over-explain simple topics. I really don't understand the high rating, he is not going to be a part of the reason you get an A.

Common exams are super hard; it's not professor-based. Ignore the previous comment, the person was probably scrolling during lectures. This professor explains the topics in detail and has amazing office hours. I will say if you can't think creatively university physics probably isn't for you. Good prof imo
maybe im insane but I dont really get the hype . he's definitely a nice person, but i did not find him to be an effective lecturer. lots of self teaching was done.

Ali Kaya is an exceptional individual and professor. He can easily explain even some of the most difficult concepts in University Physics in such a logical and focused way that as long as you try your best. Dr. Kaya will certainly set you up to succeed. In my eyes, Dr. Kaya being this good with English as his second language is truly inspirational.

Best 207 professor I could've asked for, very easy to follow especially for such a difficult subject. Exams were honestly kind of easy considering how hard some of the practice problems are. The only thing I would say is to be very careful not to get too behind.
GOAT he is the best.
He truly was an amazing 206 prof, and I would totally recommend. Exams are common so there's tons of practice and ways to prep for them! 1000% would take him again if I could
Couldn't have asked for much more from a 206 prof. He did a good job.

Took him in a 5 week course but didn't feel rushed at all. The day before each test we did a review where we could ask him to solve any problem in the past exams and that helped alot. I also suggest the summer class in you have to take it here bc it is just him making the exams not common corse so nothing should come as a surprise. DO THE HOMEWORK

I took Dr. Kaya's class in a 5 week summer course. Prior to going into this class, I had no physics knowledge and was pretty scared. He turns out to be a VERY GOOD professor/lecturer. He encourages questions even if they sound stupid. 

Fast pace, but Dr. Kaya makes the summer tests easier. Complete all homework and on time, as you need every point

The only thing your professor matters for in University Physics is for lectures (since everything else is common material), and Dr. Kaya was a very caring lecturer. He would always make sure that everyone understands the material, and was very receptive to questions. He explains concepts in class very well.

Kaya is a straight forward teacher and is understandable, which can't be said for some professors. PHYS 206 is a hard course, and this is coming from someone who took the Physics C in HS. He teaches University Physics and this past semester they took out learning objectives, which is basically a lot of partial credit. Have to study a lot for the A.

Dr. Kaya is always ready to help students with complex topics. His method of teaching is clear and understandable, but recognize that Phys 206 is not an easy A course with the increasing exam difficulty. Dr. Kaya is very understanding of students and often does reviews before exams. This course is challenging, but taking it Dr. Kaya will fare well

Like others have mentioned, Dr. Kaya is both a great lecturer and an inspirational individual. For the concepts I did struggle with, he was easy to reach outside of class even when I couldn't make any of his office hours.

It's worth noting that this class recently abandoned the Learning Objective system, so don't expect an easy A. Put in the work.

Having taken Algebra-Based Phys 1 (failed the AP Exam), Prof Kaya + past exams enabled me to learn the concepts well. He cares about students' learning and frequently asks if anybody has any questions. Mandatory attendance through iClicker. Exam 3 went poorly for me, but the final fixed everything! Make sure to do past exams, they help a lot!

All things considered, a decent professor with some crazy good lore. Explained things pretty nicely, and would do a review before each exam. However, recognize that 206 isn't an easy by any means and you'd still have to put in a lot of your own time asides from paying attention in lectures/reviewing notes to pass now that exams are more difficult.

Amazing professor, especially compared to some things ive heard from other students. I found it hard to see the big picture in this class because of how example heavy the lectures were, so if you get below a 70 ish on the first exam, pay for Spartan tutoring online video bank. not an ad guys. using it for the final and its saving me.
Great prof, he explained concepts quite clearly and simply. He definitely cared for his students and loved answering questions. Very inspirational backstory too. Would take again for sure

207 is a difficult class but Kaya is one of the best professors you can get. His lectures were rarely very confusing and he loves to answer questions. Example problems are worked out in class that can be very helpful when trying to do the Pearson homework that is almost unnecessarily difficult. Tests have a good amount of partial credit.
Very good prof, this is a tough class but he seems like he cares about student success.

Had a death in the family (an excused absence by the University) and he fought so hard to let me make up my exam. Decided on his terms that moving the exam 2 days for me was "an unreasonable amount of time". Was a decent lecturer and seemed nice until this.

Love this guy! Always felt like I was learning in the lectures. Start homeworks at least a week before the due date- it's a lot and it's hard. Don't worry if you do bad on an exam and have a bad grade- the final fixes everything if you try. Work out the past exams- they're super similar.

A great lecturer but the professor you have doesn't really matter for this class as everything is common across all sections. Inspiring story and always willing to answer questions during class. Highly recommend.

University physics with Kaya is definitely the move. I did poorly on the first exam, but the way the class is structured is it is really easy to get your grades back up and the learning objectives are very forgiving. Kaya is brilliant and it is obvious he cares for his students.

Kaya is a good professor and goes over concepts and example problems in lecture. In this course, it is so important to space out and keep up with the homework (do 4-5 modules a day), otherwise the content will become overwhelming and too much to learn before exams. Kaya doesn't record lectures but provides good explanations.

Covers the basic ideas of each concept in class. Typically does class examples that will appear on the homework or exam. Getting a good recitation TA will definitely help your grade/understanding of the material. Don't push off the homework until the last minute.

Dr. Kaya is awesome! He goes very into depth when explaining concepts which prepares you well for the exams. University Phys 206 is very standardized so no matter what professor you have you are responsible for majority of your learning. Dr. Kaya is so understanding and the nicest professor I have ever had. Also cracks jokes here and there.

Dr. Kaya has to be the single best science teacher I have ever had. I really dreaded this class, but I have scored As on every exam (final grades aren't out yet). He has an inspirational story as well, look it up sometime. He is very humble and helpful, truly fantastic all around. I cannot praise him enough. A&M made a great choice when hiring him.

He's OK. Make sure you sit at the front of the class so you can see the whiteboard. You have to go to class to do the iClickers, worth 6% of your final grade. I could barely pay attention in class. I just made sure to understand all of the homework assignments and did 5-6 practice tests before each exam. Do homework on weekends and it's not bad.

PHYS 206 is a hard course, but Dr. Kaya makes it bearable. He is very open to questions and explains concepts well. To succeed in this course, you have to spam practice exams, because exams are like 70% of the course. The way the final is set up is that if you do good on the final, that's all that matters, so don't feel too bad if midterms go bad.

This is a very difficult class, but Kaya is probably the best option for 206. He does a lot of example problems in class but he rarely finishes the problems and they are much easier than the actual exam questions you will see, most likely because there is a new coordinator for this course that makes the common exams.

Dr. Kaya is an exceptional professor. His lectures emphasize knowing how to approach, set up, and navigate problems while leaving algebra to the students. He is insanely good at explaining concepts and orchestrating iclicker questions. I was very prepared for homeworks and exams. You can tell he cares a lot about his class and students. 100/10 prof

Good professor. Phys 207 is a tough course so you will need to do a lot of self-learning regardless of the professor. The homeworks take forever and the exams are really hard but Ali Kaya is as good as you will get. I recommend him.

Im going to start by saying 206 is an extremely hard course, but professor Kaya does his best to make it managible. There is a ton of homework, but it helps with understanding what you are doing. He often goes over examples during lectures which are helpful but can leave out some important details. You MUST learn by yourself in this course!!!

Amazing professor with amazing lectures. He is clearly very experienced with teaching physics and cares deeply about his students. His grade distribution is lower than it should be because he teaches during the off-semesters. Highly highly recommend Dr. Kaya. And look up his backstory online for an interesting and inspirational read.

To be honest, it doesn't really matter what teacher you get for university physics. You can easily self teach yourself the material and do fine on the exams. That being said, Kaya was a good professor and was very accessible and friendly when it came to understanding and asking questions.

Outstanding professor! Clear, engaging lectures foster a dynamic learning environment. Approachable and supportive, providing valuable guidance. Fair grading system emphasizes critical thinking. Highly recommend for a top-notch educational experience! 5/5 stars!
He teaches clearly. He has amazing Lectures. Awesome Professor.

His lectures are very thorough, and he makes sure to go over examples that look like the homework problems. He is willing to answer all questions to make sure we understand. He always does a review before each exam. There aren't too many problems in homework sets, but each hw problem takes a while to complete.

Great Professor. He teaches well, and is always willing to answer questions. Regardless, physics is a pretty tough topic but he makes it understandable. The only reason I didn't do well is because I really didn't pay attention until the very end of the semester, which is on me. Overall really recommend.
reviews.ratingTags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I took PHYS 206 last spring with Dr. Kaya, and he was a great professor. He teaches enthusiastically, simplifies confusing concepts, and encourages questions. His lectures are very helpful, especially for the homework (start it early each week, it can be a lot), and practice exams help a lot for this class.

Very helpful, go to office hours if you need examples or help on homework/problems. Going to lecture is good since he gives lots of examples that can be on the exams. The Final Exam can improve your grade by a lot if you are struggling on the other 3 common exams.
Great prof, he has a very inspirational backstory, if you have the chance, ask about it during office hours. Make sure to sit in the front and take notes if you want to get an A.
reviews.ratingTags: Amazing lectures --Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: If you have to take him, don't make the mistake of taking him at 8 AM. The lectures are enough to put you to sleep any hour of the day, but the homework assignments and tests were fairly easy. I would definitely recommend university physics since the tests are more number-oriented and are much more tolerable than Don't Panic physics.

Great dude, but rarely finishes problems all the way through. Extremely intelligent and answers class questions well, but lectures often left me confused about the algebra of example problems since he rarely would work through a problem all the way to a final answer.

Dr. Kaya is extremely knowledgeable and funny, and taking him will set you up for success in University Physics. Make sure you attend recitation and do your clicker questions, and you should do well in the class.

Dr Kaya is the best professor I've had so far at tamu, ima freshman going into engineering rn. If you can take Kaya - he has some super cool stories about him and is super super knowledgeable and accessible about all of the content. You don't really have to go to class just do the iclickers at the right time, but you should, he makes class fun.

He has a kinda heavy accent but is a good teacher. I knew a lot of the physics before taking the class but his lectures were still pretty good. He did do a lot of practice problems during lectures. The homeworks were annoying and long but not too bad. I didn't even touch the textbook all year.
Professor has a heavy accent. Read the textbook before going to class. He goes over complicated problems, so know the basics before class. Ask questions!

I took this class over the summer and loved Dr Kaya. His lectures are amazing and he posted all of them. He encourages asking questions and is very available for office hours. There was a lot of homework but nothing crazy for a STEM class. The exams are very similar to the practice tests and homework. Attendance was mandatory low weight.
reviews.ratingTags: Amazing lectures --Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment:
*Taken for Summer Class*

Professor Kaya is understanding and very nice to his students, I found his lectures entertaining and straight to the point. He made this class easy even with the summer hell schedule. Take him if you can during the summer.

Dr. Kaya taught the info extremely well and would leave an entire day before the exam for Q&A, where he would answer any questions we had. Throughout his lectures he would always stop to answer a person's question, and he always made people feel welcome to ask. The content is difficult but he provides the resources (past exams and mp) to succeed.

This was my second time taking this class, and it went so much better than the first. I went from a D to a B+. He actually taught the material very well compared to other professors here at A&M. I actually understood what was going on in this class without the textbook thanks to him. He preps you well too for exams. If you can, take his class!!

Throughout the summer course for professor Kaya, I showed up regularly to both his lectures and recitation and was able to keep a high A. His lectures were interesting and he was very open to receiving questions throughout and made sure to answer your question to the best of his ability. I don't think I would've done as well, if not for him.

HIGHLY recommend Dr. Kaya. You will have to work hard in any Physics section you take, but his HW and recitations are helpful. He actively encourages asking questions in class and will answer even the simplest questions with clear and thorough detail until you understand. Very approachable and reachable, which is so necessary for this class.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Ali Kaya has an accent but its not thick at all. I think he taches the basics really well, but you will need outside help to do really well in the course. Make smart friends, pay attention in class, and try to do the homework

Dr. Kaya was a great professor. Although his lectures were hard to follow at times, he effectively answered any questions with great feedback. Homework was a bit tedious but if done correctly it can help your understanding of course material and will definitely help on exams. Attendance is taken through iclicker so definitely go to class.

Dr. Kaya is one of the best professors when it comes to University Physics. He encourages asking questions and is ready to answer whatever questions you may have. He tries to teach as clearly as possible with few confusions. He does his job to the fullest and it is up to the student to get the grade they deserve.

Professor Kaya is a very kind and approachable person who really tries his best to make each student understand the material. His lectures are to the point and he encourages students to ask questions. I highly recommend taking advantage of his office hours if you are struggling since he will explain problems in depth and clear up any confusion.

Kaya the GOAT. Contains his big chad energy in a nice and humble manner. He teaches all the content appropriately in a way that makes sense. He does test reviews before exams where you are free to answer questions you have if you don't see him outside of class. Very good/10.

Professor Kaya wrote out basic problems on the board which was hard to read. The problems were super easy and not reflective of what was actually tested. The tests had a lot of partial credit but the problems were terribly written. He also was not easily accessible outside of class and I didn't feel like I could talk to him.
Good professor. Many may find him to be a boring lecturer, but he teaches the subject well, and knows his stuff.

Professor Kaya clearly cares about his students. He encourages a lot of questions. Unfortunately, he teaches very slow. We didn't always finish the content in time, which makes homework a nightmare. I would have had to do extensive self-teaching had I not had a solid physics foundation coming out of high school. Good man, not a great professor.

When he's teaching you can tell he really knows what he's talking about. He loves when you ask questions and is eager to teach. He's good at breaking things down if you ask and overall a nice guy who really does care about his students and their grades. Not an easy A (any physics usually isn't) but willing to work with you one on one. MC exams!!
